clue.text: Allotment failure of a tenant farmer ?

parts.note: an allotment is a portion handed out, a share
to come a cropper is to fail badly, so a cropper is a failure

explanation.surface: A man renting land sees his garden plot fail.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets 'Allotment' up as a British garden plot; here it is a portion handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharecropper works rented land and pays the owner with part of the harvest.

clue.text: Lead follower away from work-seen at Lord's ?

definitions.meaning: one who swings the lead, an idler dodging work by feigning illness
a bowler or delivery that swings in the air, a sight at a cricket ground

explanation.walkthrough: To swing the lead is British slang for shirking. Lord's is the famous London cricket ground, where swing bowling is common.
explanation.definitionFit: A shirker is said to swing the lead, and a cricket bowler who moves the ball in flight is a swing bowler.

clue.text: Sought ingredient for dish such as kedgeree

indicators.note: an ingredient sits inside a dish, so the letters lie within these words

explanation.surface: Someone wanted a component for a rice-and-fish breakfast dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Kedgeree is a British dish of rice, smoked fish and eggs; the run sits across 'such as kedgeree'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have sought something is to have requested it.

clue.text: A bloomer we see as wrong Wilde sees …

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are put wrong, that is jumbled

explanation.surface: We spot a blunder that Oscar Wilde also notices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a mistake, but it is a flowering plant; 'we see' is link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: The edelweiss is an Alpine flowering plant, and a bloomer can mean anything that flowers.

clue.text: …as right as this by Maugham

definitions.meaning: the idiom 'right as ...' means perfectly fine
a short story by Somerset Maugham, later filmed

explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues the previous one's ellipsis; the two halves point to an idiom and a story title.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'right as rain' completes the first part, and Somerset Maugham wrote a famous short story of that title.

clue.text: Queues for tobacco ?

definitions.meaning: a queue is an old word for a plait of hair hanging at the back
twisted tobacco sold in a thin rope

explanation.walkthrough: 'Queues' suggests lines of people waiting, but it means plaits of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaited hair hanging down the back and a twisted rope of chewing tobacco share the name.

clue.text: City Road bird takes your money

definitions.text: City Road bird takes your money

parts.words: City Road bird takes your money
parts.note: the nursery rhyme 'Pop goes the weasel' runs 'up and down the City Road, in and out the' pub of that bird's name, 'that's the way the money goes'

explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme names a London pub on City Road, where the money goes; the pub is named after a bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's London pub on City Road is named after this large bird of prey, where drinkers spent their money.

clue.text: Phony admission of poverty takes in a good man

indicators.note: one piece swallows the other, holding it within

parts.note: someone admitting poverty says I'M POOR
ST, saint, is the crossword good man

explanation.surface: A fraud pleads poverty while sheltering a decent fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A phony as a noun is a fake person, one who pretends to be somebody else.

clue.text: Prohibition has no backing from Hindu trader

parts.note: a prohibition is a ban

indicators.note: backing means the word for no is read from its back end

parts.note: nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: A ban gets no support from an Indian merchant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns NAY to YAN; the surface reads it as support.
explanation.definitionFit: A banyan was a Hindu trader or merchant in India, the source of the tree's name.

clue.text: Suitable for sound public entertainment

indicators.note: the phrase is heard rather than spelt, so its spoken form is taken

parts.note: running a pub, entertaining the public, is innkeeping

explanation.surface: Something fitting as a decent show for the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning good; it signals that innkeeping, a landlord's trade of entertaining the public, is heard as the two-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in keeping is appropriate, matching its surroundings.

clue.text: Part of a plant looks grand to Miss Woodhouse

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
Emma Woodhouse is the heroine of Jane Austen's novel Emma

explanation.surface: Jane Austen's heroine admires a fine flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A gemma is a bud or small detachable body by which some plants reproduce.

clue.text: Sink warehouse?

definitions.meaning: to sink is to descend, to go under
in South and East Asia a storehouse is called by this Anglo-Indian name

explanation.definitionFit: To descend is to go under the surface, and in India and East Asia a storage building at a port has this Anglo-Indian name.

clue.text: Broken toy Grace brought to class

indicators.note: a broken toy is in pieces, and the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Grace brings her damaged plaything to school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class' suggests a school lesson; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A class is a group or division, a kind of thing.

clue.text: Airmen, if returning a tie…

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, are airmen

indicators.note: returning means the little word if is read backwards

explanation.surface: Air force men, coming back, wonder about a necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffia is palm fibre used by gardeners to tie up plants.

clue.text: Well-known spirit of Endor

definitions.meaning: the Witch of Endor in the Bible is said to have had a ... spirit, a demon companion

explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible Saul consults the Witch of Endor, a woman with a familiar spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well known is commonplace to us, and a witch's attendant demon is her familiar spirit.

clue.text: .that comes adrift mainly from drawing careless knot

parts.note: a plan is a drawing

indicators.note: a careless knot comes undone, so the word knot is rearranged

explanation.surface: Something slips loose because it was drawn with a sloppy knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' is the trick: not 'mostly' but 'on the main', the open sea, where tiny organisms drift.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are tiny organisms that drift in the sea rather than swim.

clue.text: Henry got air-van repaired

indicators.note: a repaired van has been put back together, the letters newly arranged

explanation.surface: Henry had his flying van fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like any man; it is Prince Henry the Navigator of Portugal, who sponsored voyages of exploration.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Henry of Portugal, patron of fifteenth-century voyages of discovery, is known by this epithet.

clue.text: Work of composer Roger as patchy as theirs?

definitions.text: Work of composer Roger as patchy as theirs?

parts.words: Work of composer Roger as patchy as theirs?
parts.note: the English composer Roger Quilter is mocked as uneven, like the work of people who sew patchwork bedcovers

explanation.walkthrough: Roger Quilter was an English song composer; patchwork covers are made by sewing patches.
explanation.definitionFit: People who make patchwork bedspreads produce literally patchy work, and the composer Roger shares their surname.

clue.text: Substance of yarn a famous medium told

parts.note: Daniel Dunglas Home was a famous Victorian spiritualist medium
a yarn that is told is spun

explanation.surface: The gist of a tall story a celebrated psychic related.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' seems to be a story, and 'told' plays on that; really the definition is cloth woven from yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun is coarse cloth woven from yarn spun at home.

clue.text: Plain vessel of internal elm construction

indicators.note: the vessel's construction is internal, built inside it

parts.note: a hoy is a small coastal sailing vessel

indicators.note: construction means the letters of elm are built into a new order

explanation.surface: A simple boat built inside from elm wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction' turns ELM into MEL, which goes inside HOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain here means unattractive or homespun, as in an ordinary-looking face.

clue.text: Reluctant to use a metrical form

parts.note: verse is writing in metre

explanation.surface: A poet unwilling to write in a set metre.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disinclined to do something is being opposed to it.

clue.text: State paper

definitions.meaning: to state is to put into words
the Daily ... is a British newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Express is a British national newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something is to put it into words, and the Daily Express is a British national newspaper.

clue.text: Massive structure ? Poor clue for very small matter

parts.note: a mole is a huge stone breakwater

indicators.note: a poor clue needs mending, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bad clue for something tiny next to something huge.
explanation.walkthrough: A mole is a massive stone pier or breakwater, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A molecule is a tiny particle of a substance, the smallest unit keeping its chemistry.

clue.text: Company of soldiers turned up one in a fur coat

parts.note: Coy is the military abbreviation for a company of soldiers

indicators.note: turned means the little word up is reversed

explanation.surface: A troop of soldiers appeared with someone wearing a fur.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American rodent with valuable fur, so it is an animal wearing a fur coat.

clue.text: Supporter of what's laid on board

definitions.text: Supporter of what's laid on board

parts.words: Supporter of what's laid on board
parts.note: board means a breakfast table; the item holds up something a hen has laid

explanation.walkthrough: 'board' looks like a ship or plank but is a table, and 'laid' a hen's egg not a place setting.
explanation.definitionFit: This small cup holds a boiled hen's product at breakfast.

clue.text: Preservers told to proceed by this rule

parts.note: people preserving food are told to tin it, the imperative can
on means forward, proceed

explanation.surface: Food preservers are instructed to carry on following this regulation.
explanation.walkthrough: The instruction to preservers is 'can on!', keep tinning.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a rule or law, especially one of the Church.

clue.text: Artisan's guides to dances

definitions.meaning: a workman's jig is a device guiding a tool

explanation.definitionFit: Craftsmen use templates called jigs to guide tools, and jigs are lively folk dances.

clue.text: Like the wood, for instance, used for making longer tables ?

definitions.text: Like the wood, for instance, used for making longer tables ?

parts.words: Like the wood, for instance, used for making longer tables ?
parts.note: a wood is full of foliage, and the hinged extra flaps that lengthen a dining table share that foliage word

explanation.walkthrough: A table's extension flaps are called leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood is full of foliage, and an extending table has removable flaps called leaves.

clue.text: Being sixteen, changed denomination

indicators.note: changed means the letters of sixteen are rearranged

parts.note: CE, the Church of England, is a denomination

explanation.definitionFit: Being as a noun is the state of living or having reality.

clue.text: Financial controller's holdings

parts.note: holdings read as the cords that hold a money bag shut, the grip on spending

explanation.walkthrough: 'holdings' suggests investments, but means the cords that close a purse; whoever holds them controls spending.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever holds the cords of a money pouch controls spending.
